source: Nevertheless, they're all outhanded. I changed the letter to order them killed instead.
But how? Certainly it bore the King's seal?
I still have my father's signet ring. It was simple. Alarmingly so.
...Then we were besieged by pirates just outside the sound—and they took me as their hostage.
...Pirates? Surely you cannot be serious.
Extraordinarily serious, Horatio.
Once they learned my identity, I promised to send them a good fortune and safe harbor if they deposited me here. And so they have.
So Rosie and Guil are—dead?
If not now, then when they reach England. They'll perish then. Just as they wanted for me.
Horatio—with all that's happening—who doesn't want me dead? Who can I trust?
Me, your lordship.
Of that I have no doubt. And Ophelia has made her hatred towards me quite clear.
In that way, she's safe as well. Better a former paramour turned sour than one whose alignment is ambiguous.
That's why I summoned you both, to make you aware that my return to Denmark is one great intent.
In my heart there's been a kind of fighting that won't let me sleep.
I shall no longer hesitate in bringing down my uncle.
He that killed my King and whored my mother, popping between the election and my hopes...
I cannot let this canker of our nature come to further evil.
H-Hamlet, you know, Laertes has a standing challenge to duel you. I believe the King is behind it somehow.
Of course, Horatio. And of course, I cannot refuse, as they both well know. It is intended to murder me, not to out any honor of mine.
Divinity shapes our ends. So be it, friends. We'll duel.
Is this a skull...?
My lord, you mustn't touch that, I can't imagine how filthy it—er—
I recognize him! Yorick!
I knew him, Horatio. A fellow of infinite jest. When I was a boy, he used to give me rides on his back.
And now he's dead. His flesh is rotten.
Hamlet, please. Let me take that from you.
Hamlet, you son of a bitch.
Where is my father's body? What have you done with it?
Certainly I am much too mad to know... hee hee.
I hate you, Hamlet. I've always hated you.
Well, at least Yorick liked me. Tit for tat.
...You're not making any sense.
You've ruined my father's honor and stolen my sister's happiness. Hamlet, stand up to me like a man.
A man! Is that what I am?
Very well. What do I care if I live or not?
A duel. You. At 11 sharp. We'll settle this for good.
All right. I'm here.
You're late.
Take Laertes' hand, as gentlemen do.
(Shall we improvise?)
(He cannot know anything is amiss. Play your part.)
My lord, a moment, please. There is a point which must be made. I've wronged you most grievously.
All the wrong I've done you lately—all the insult I've borne you—it was madness. I've not been in my right mind.
Listen. I'm sorry for all of it. Or rather, my madness itself can offer an apology. And if I'm truly as mad as everyone says I am...
No. I won't use that as an excuse. I killed a man. I did something I can never take back. And for that, no apology is enough.
Is this remorse? From Hamlet? I can hardly believe what I'm hearing, truth be told.
Laertes, we've fought forever. And none of it ever came to anything useful or good. I've been a fool for so long.
We share a brotherly bond in some ways. We've fought like siblings. And I'm... I miss your father. I loved him, though I was poor at showing it.
You mean, even though you murdered him.
No. I understand. I accept your apology, Hamlet. But something must be done to preserve my honor here. You understand.
We can't call the whole thing off. We've done the work to gather everyone here. We need some sort of show, don't we?
Come, now. Let's skirmish like we did as children. One final time before our final peace.
I like the sound of that.
My lord Claudius, this blade is too heavy, methinks. I'll need another.
Of course. Kubilius, will you hand him mine?
(And I'll prepare a fitting draught, should Hamlet's thirst run strong...)
Now. On the third count.
This is exhausting to watch. I need a drink.
This isn't going to end well. I can feel it.
I'm sure Hamlet won't mind if I sip from his goblet.
I'm sure Hamlet won't mind if I sip from his—
Ahh. Cool wine on a summer day. Something wrong, my love?
O-oh—I feel unwell.
Please, my son. Caution!
En garde, Hamlet.
Touché, Laertes.
Ngh. Likewise.
And I made a mark with your own blade, at that! Maybe I'm not half so awful a swordsman as I thought...
(How did he nick me? T-that's the poisoned one!)
(Ergh. He's been practicing.)
I submit, my lord.
My love, a-are you—look at me—are you all right?
The... grrgh... the drink...
The drink is—poisoned. Hamlet, poison—
Guards, one of you help my lady, immediately!
Although if it is poison, we're too late.
W-what? What villainy is this?
Mother... She's turning pale...
No, no, no-- this cannot be! It cannot be real, can it?
Who would have done something like this? Whoever it is, I'll kill them!
Gertrude's dead? It all happened so fast.
You may not submit.
Play on until this fated duel has run its course.
It was me, Hamlet.
The blade was poisoned from the start of our duel. There's not half an hour of life left in you.
No medicine in the world can do either of us good now. Or her, for that matter.
No medicine in the world can do either of us good now.
We're all dead. And the King is to blame. It's all useless now.
I'm sorry to you. And to you, Ophelia. I... guess I won't be... able to take Father's place for you after all.
I wish when the King told me his plans, I had come to my senses.
Then it's too late for the both of us. But not too late to make things right.
You did this.
H-Hamlet, be reasonable—
No. You've taken my father, my mother, my crown, and soon my life from me.
No. You've taken my father, my crown, and soon my life from me.
You murdered my father in cold blood. I heard you confess it yourself.
You've stolen everything I've ever loved in this life. You've robbed me of my ability to feel joy, to want anything good.
But I'm not dead yet, Claudius. There's still time for one last thing. Venom, do your work.
Then come and destroy me, Hamlet. You've always wanted this.
No. You're being manipulated.
By him. He's the one who ought to pay for his crimes.
You did this, Claudius.
But I'm not dead yet, Claudius. There's still time to do one last thing.
Now's our chance, Hamlet. Take back the crown.
...At last.
Soon, my father can finally rest.
Uncle... it's time to atone for your sins.
Venom, to thy work.
Help! Help, guards, he's run me through, but I--I--augh...
He's justly served. Hamlet, listen...
My father's death wasn't your fault. Nor mine. I want you to—ngh—to know that.
And Ophelia-- you know-- I-- it--
I know. I love you, Laertes.
How did this happen?
Listen, Horatio. There isn't much time, old friend.
You have to survive. Tell everyone what happened here.
I don't think I can, Hamlet. I'm more an antique Roman than a Dane. I'd rather die with my captain.
The wine... there's still some poison left. Let me be with you.
That blade... there's still some poison left. Let me be with you.
Don't you dare. If you ever loved me, Horatio, as I do you...
Then you'll have to wait to join me. And I hope it's years. Long, happy years.
I need you to tell the story of what we went through. Don't let all this be in vain.
And... Fortinbras... I can hear his men approaching now...
The election lights on him. He'll be King. I believe it in my heart. The rest is silence.
...He's fainted.
Fools. All of them.
Perhaps he played his part a little too well.
Claudius... He's dead!
The time has come, Mother. Peace has come to Elsinore.
Mother. I'm sorry.
Excellent. Excellent. Watch your footing, Laertes.
(At this rate, I may not need this goblet at all.)
(One way or another, this will come to an end soon.)
Get on with it!
If you insist.
The castle clock just struck midnight.
Did I survive? Is it over?
I don't hear anything. Perhaps the invasion was turned away.
Maybe it's done. Maybe I've ended the loop for good...
Oh-- my head hurts--
Pulled back through time.

source: Ergh—here it comes—
What was that?
It came from the Great Hall.
I hear a commotion. The castle's being stormed again.
It's just outside the doors of the hall.
For those of you who have not made Our acquaintance: We are Prince Fortinbras of Norway.
Now, stand down, Denmark. The day is won before you have carried forth.
After all, it seems your new King met with an unfortunate fate.
You mean-- Hamlet?
He could have accepted Our offer of peace and unity.
Instead, warlike as he was, he insisted on attempting to match Us. And he lost.
(Hamlet. You idiot. I knew it would come to this.)
(You were so close to being the man your country needed.)
Prince Fortinbras? What are you doing here? We had an agreement.
Unfortunately for you, your own country's nobility made a far better one.
Prince Fortinbras. I liked you better in our dungeon.
No one must die, Claudius.
Declare your fealty to Us, and We will leave you with some small status. We are not a savage ruler.
Declare fealty to you? A boy no older than my nephew?
I wrested this throne to my hand on the labors of my own sweat and ambition. I will hand it to no one!
My lady, you are his wife. As I understand it, you are beloved by your people. Can you speak no sense to him?
You speak to me so kindly, but assume I will be pliant to you. So long as my husband lives, Denmark is ours. I will die to keep it so.
Very well. You sign your own death warrants. So be it.
Men, to arms.
Prince Hamlet. Perhaps you will prove yourself wiser. Wise enough, perhaps, to submit peacefully.
Stand down?
Your father killed Our father. Now, young Prince, what's yours must return to Our hands.
But this need not be a bloody coup.
No one must die. Surrender peacefully, and you will be permitted to sit the throne.
So long, of course, as you swear your undying fealty to Ours and to Norway.
As the Queen of this castle, I now represent its interests and rule.
We will submit to you.
With my husband and son gone, I see little other choice which preserves the life that remains here.
My queen, we can't simply roll over!
